newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE CONTINUE TO MAKE ENGLAND TOIL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE CONTINUE TO MAKE ENGLAND TOIL.

text.p: A lacklustre bowling performance by England let Zimbabwe off the hook on the second day of the inaugural test match between the two countries at Queen's Club on Thursday.
England picked up just one wicket in the session and by lunch Zimbabwe had progressed from their overnight 256 for six to 337 for seven in 123 overs.
A seventh wicket stand of 79 in less than two hours between Andy Flower and Paul Strang put the hosts into a commanding position.

Strang hit two boundaries in the second over of the day bowled by Robert Croft to set the tone. He was eventually caught off a slow full toss from Chris Silverwood for 38, having hit seven boundaries in a 69-ball stay.
Flower was poised for his third test century at the interval. Resuming on 58, he has so far ground out 94 from 287 balls with 10 fours, an innings of immense value to Zimbabwe.
